newsitem.title: JAPAN: NTT says plans low-cost Internet access service.
newsitem.headline: NTT says plans low-cost Internet access service.

text.p: Japanese telecommunications giant Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT) said on Wednesday it plans to start a low-cost Internet access service in December for individual users in Tokyo.
It plans to apply soon to the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications for permission to launch the service, a company official said.

Its Open Computer Network (OCN) service will allow users to access the Internet over existing phone lines for up to 15 hours a month for 2,300 yen ($20), less than the cost of most other such services available in Japan.

As part of the OCN service, NTT also plans to lay dedicated lines for low-speed computer network transmissions from December. It said dedicated lines would be more economical for those using the Internet for more than 50 hours a month.

The dedicated line service will first be offered in just two regional cities, Fujisawa in Kanagawa Prefecture and Ogaki in Gifu, but will be expanded early next year to 11 other cities, including Tokyo.
The service will cost 37,000 yen ($333) a month, about half the cost users now pay for a dedicated line, an NTT spokesman said.

"Japan's communication fees have been criticised for being too high, but our new service will help narrow the price gaps with foreign countries substantially," Masamichi Tanabe, an NTT executive, told a news conference. ($1=111 yen)
